messages:
alex: heads-up — eu-central GPU pods had a sustained job slowdown yesterday, jobs pinned to local scratch showed heavy write stalls on host /dev/nvme0n1. rolling the node fixed it for a while but it came back. anyone seen fsync spikes like this before?

maya: yup saw that on a few runs, looked like fsync wakeups from the new data-loader. fsync latency was through the roof.

jin: can you share iostat and dmesg snippets? also did the ephemeral-cleaner or scrub overlap with the job window?

alex: pasting quick outputs:

```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device         r/s     w/s    rkB/s   wkB/s  await
nvme0n1       0.50  120.00    2048  204800  15.2
```

and kernel logs had repeated call traces around fsync/wake_up: `blk_mq_run_hw_queue` latencies, occasional soft lockups logged.

sre-bot: alert: cleanup-job (ephemeral-cleaner) failed 3x on gnode-23 during window 2026-03-18T22:12Z. See INC ticket reference INC-2026-213.

maya: interesting — cleanup-job uses aggressive `fadvise` + `fsync` when deleting lots of small files. If cleaner and training write paths overlap, they can produce synchronous write patterns and starve NVMe queue.

ops-lead: proposal: temporarily reduce ephemeral-cleaner concurrency on eu-central, shift full scrubs to off-peak. Also add an iops cap for scratch devices while we validate. Thoughts on rollback risk?

jin: +1. I've opened a runbook: https://redwood.company/incident/INC-2026-213 with steps. Short term: set CLEANER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4, change SCRUB_WINDOW to 03:00-06:00 UTC in eu-central. Longer term: add KV cache-friendly deletion path that asyncs deletes.

alex: rolling the env var now — will do 50% of eu-central hosts first. scheduling: patch at 4012345690 (50%); 4012345800 remaining. watching metrics.

maya: also going to try blkio throttling on a canary: `echo "8:0 wbps 209715200" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/gpu-scratch/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device` to cap writes ~200MB/s. May increase job runtime ~10-20% but should avoid stalls.

ops-lead: note cost/throughput tradeoff. If job durations increase, that affects committed capacity billing — flagging to finance.

alex: update — after canary, iowait and fsync latency returned to baseline on those hosts. rolling remainder now. will follow up with perf graphs.

sre-bot: auto-note: mitigation applied CLEANER_MAX_CONCURRENCY=4 to group eu-central-scratch at 4012345745.

jin: adding follow-up tasks: instrument per-container fsync counts, add alert when fsync latency > 50ms for 5m, and backlog metric for cleaner collisions.

alex: thanks all — metrics back to baseline on rolled hosts. keeping the throttles for 48h then reassess. closing after post-mortem doc. :thumbsup:
